data.proposedArchitecture:
Build the shell INSIDE the existing rectify-kmp repository and relocate this spec's `.pipeline/` SDD workspace there, so spec, code and the design system live in one git repo. Rationale from reading the code, not from theory: rectify-kmp does not merely hold a token file set — `presentation-core-styling` (31 files: ThemeColor/ThemeSpacing/ThemeTypography/ThemeRadius/ThemeCorner/ThemeStroke/ThemeMotion/ThemeSize + `AppTheme` already resolving ThemeMode.Light/Dark/System via `isSystemInDarkTheme()`) is paired with `presentation-core-ui` (109 files) that ALREADY contains Rectify-specific, style-guide-authored components for exactly this shell: `SidebarTabs`/`SidebarTabItem` (whose own KDoc example is `Annotations 3 · Payload · History 1`), `SegmentedButtonGroup` (the Android|iOS toolbar switch), `DeviceChip` + `DeviceChipState` (the `● No device ▾` indicator), `CounterBadge` (`⓪ staged`), `StatusLine`/`StatusStep`/`FeedbackBar` (the status bar), `StatusIndicator`, `StatusPill`, `KeyCap` (`⌘↵`), `AppButton`, `SourceListRow`, `CommandBlock`, `RectifyLogo`, plus annotation/measure components for downstream specs. The desktop runnable path already exists end to end (`:desktop-application` plain-JVM module → `Main.kt` → `initKoin()` → `compose-application/desktopMain/runDesktopApp()` → `application { Window { App() } }`), and the theme-persistence chain already exists end to end (`ThemePreferenceSourceImpl.KEY_THEME = "pref_theme"` → `ThemePreferenceMapper` → `ConfigureRepository.observe/get/setTheme` → `ObserveThemeUseCase` → `App.kt` mapping ThemeModel→ThemeMode), backed on desktop by `PreferencesSettings(Preferences.userRoot().node("dev.rectify.io"))`. Rebuilding or porting any of that into an empty `/Users/andrew-malitchuk/Documents/rectify` is a fork of ~140 source files, which is a direct, permanent threat to NFR-9/AC-30/AC-36 ("adopted as-is, unmodified").

Shell shape inside that repo — three additions, NO new Gradle module:
1. `presentation-core-ui/source/kit/organism/shell/` — the slot contract: `RectifyWindowShell`, `ShellToolbar`, `ShellStatusBar`, `StageSurface`, `SidePanelFrame`, `PanelResizeHandle` (atom), `ShellTab` enum, `rememberShellState`. All stateless/hoisted, previewable under `AppTheme { }` per `.claude/rules/compose-preview-convention.md`, reading tokens only from `@Composable` scope via `Theme.*` per `.claude/rules/design-tokens.md` (zero `Color(0x...)`, zero raw `.dp` at call sites). Layering: `PanelResizeHandle` is an atom; `ShellStatusBar` composes existing molecules; `RectifyWindowShell`/`ShellToolbar`/`SidePanelFrame` are organisms — no atom reaches upward.
2. `compose-application/desktopMain/.../window/` — `runDesktopApp()` extended with `rememberWindowState(size = DpSize(1240.dp, 820.dp))` (FR-17/AC-34), `window.minimumSize = Dimension(1024, 700)` set inside the `FrameWindowScope` (Compose Desktop's `Window` exposes no `minimumSize` parameter — it must go through the AWT window), macOS full-size-content client properties for the traffic-light inset, `onPreviewKeyEvent` for Cmd+1/2/3 (FR-16/AC-33), and `AppTheme(mode = resolvedMode)` wrapping `RectifyWindowShell` filled with stub slots (AC-37).
3. `data-preference-api`/`-impl` + repository/use-case chain — ONE new preference, `pref_side_panel_width` (Int dp), following the existing `pref_<name>` convention (FR-21/AC-39); theme reuses the existing `pref_theme` key unchanged (the preferences rule forbids changing an existing key), with the only behavioural change being the first-launch default flipping from `ThemeModel.Light` to System (FR-18/AS-5) — ideally by renaming the misleading `ThemeModel.MaterialU` entry to `ThemeModel.System` while keeping its stored string value intact.

State management: plain Compose state hoisting (`rememberShellState` holding `activeTab` + `panelWidth`, `isSessionActive` passed in), NOT Orbit MVI. `.claude/rules/orbit-mvi.md` is scoped by frontmatter to `presentation-feature-*/**`; the shell is a layout organism plus a window entry point, with three fields, no async work, no navigation side effects and no error states. A `ContainerHost` + Contract/ViewModel/Screen/Content quartet here would be four files of ceremony around `var activeTab by remember`. Persisted values (theme, panel width) are read at the window root through the existing Koin use cases, exactly as `App.kt` already reads theme today.
highLevelPlan: Decide the repository/token strategy FIRST (survey Q1) — everything else depends on it; recommendation: relocate the SDD `.pipeline/` workspace into rectify-kmp and build there.
Establish the shell's slot contract as the deliverable's real API surface: RectifyWindowShell(toolbar, stage, sidePanel?, statusBar) with hoisted panel width and active tab.

Reuse presentation-core-ui's existing Rectify components for every toolbar/status-bar/side-panel part instead of authoring new ones; add only what is genuinely missing (shell organism, resize handle, stage ground).
Wire theme through the already-shipped AppTheme/ThemeMode + pref_theme chain, changing only the first-launch default to System (FR-18/AS-5).
Add exactly one new persisted value (pref_side_panel_width) for FR-21/AC-39.

Establish the repo's FIRST test suite (none exists today) around the shell's pure logic plus an automated WCAG contrast assertion over both shipped palettes — this converts several inspection-only ACs into runnable checks.
Keep every slot stubbed (AC-37): no adb/idb, no device state, no tab content.

components.name: RectifyWindowShell (organism, presentation-core-ui)
components.responsibility: THE slot contract. `RectifyWindowShell(toolbar: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit, stage: @Composable BoxScope.() -> Unit, sidePanel: (@Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)? = null, statusBar: @Composable RowScope.() -> Unit, panelWidth: Dp, onPanelWidthChange: (Dp) -> Unit, onPanelResizeEnd: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier)`. Column[toolbar | Row[stage(weight 1f) | handle | panel(panelWidth)] | statusBar] on `Theme.color.bg`. `sidePanel == null` renders no panel and no handle — the AC-31/FR-15 pre-mirror state is expressed by nullability, not by a boolean flag, so downstream features cannot accidentally render an empty panel.

components.name: ShellToolbar (organism)
components.responsibility: Full-width `Theme.color.chrome` bar with a bottom `Theme.color.line` hairline. Six named slots in screenshot order: `trafficLightInset` (reserved width only), `platformSwitch`, `deviceIndicator`, spacer, `stagedCounter`, `clear`, `primaryAction`. Named slots (not a free-form RowScope) so downstream specs cannot reorder the canonical toolbar.

components.name: ShellStatusBar (organism)
components.responsibility: Full-width bottom bar, top hairline, `leading` and `trailing` slots. Stub fills: `StatusIndicator`/`StatusLine` with static `adb 35.0.1 · idb 1.1.8 · ready` (monoMeta) left, `Rectify 0.4` right (FR-13/AC-37). Hosts the theme-override control (see ThemeOverrideToggle).

components.name: StageSurface (organism)
components.responsibility: The bezel-less stage: fills all space between toolbar and status bar, `Theme.color.stage` ground with the subtle dotted-grid texture drawn in a Canvas from tokens (FR-14). Takes a content slot — the NO SIGNAL card and the 'Waiting for an Android device' copy are downstream content, the ground and the empty-state frame are shell.

components.name: SidePanelFrame (organism)
components.responsibility: Fixed-width column: `SidebarTabs` header (REUSED from presentation-core-ui, items Notes/Payload/History) + a content slot keyed by `ShellTab`. Defaults to `ShellTab.Notes` on first appearance (FR-16/AC-32). Tab CONTENT is a slot — out of scope (AC-12 is about the three tabs existing).

components.name: PanelResizeHandle (atom)
components.responsibility: ~4dp visual hairline (`Theme.color.line2`) inside a ~8dp hit area; `Modifier.draggable(Horizontal)` emitting dp deltas, `pointerHoverIcon(E_RESIZE_CURSOR)`, `onDragStopped` callback. Clamping is NOT done here — it is done by `clampPanelWidth`, so it is unit-testable without a UI.

components.name: clampPanelWidth(current: Dp, delta: Dp): Dp (pure function)
components.responsibility: `(current + delta).coerceIn(PANEL_MIN_WIDTH /*260.dp*/, PANEL_MAX_WIDTH /*480.dp*/)`. The entire AC-38 acceptance surface in one testable function.

components.name: ShellTab enum + shortcutToTab(isMeta: Boolean, key: Key): ShellTab? (pure function)
components.responsibility: `Notes/Payload/History` and the Cmd+1/2/3 mapping (FR-16/AC-33). Pure so Stage 5 can assert it; the `onPreviewKeyEvent` wiring itself is verified by inspection.

components.name: rememberShellState (state holder)
components.responsibility: `class ShellState(initialPanelWidth: Dp) { var activeTab by mutableStateOf(ShellTab.Notes); var panelWidth by mutableStateOf(initialPanelWidth) }`. Plain Compose state hoisting — no Orbit container, no ViewModel.

components.name: RectifyWindow (compose-application / desktopMain)
components.responsibility: Owns `rememberWindowState(size = DpSize(1240.dp, 820.dp))`, sets `window.minimumSize = Dimension(1024, 700)` in a `LaunchedEffect` inside `FrameWindowScope`, applies the macOS title-bar client properties, installs `onPreviewKeyEvent`, resolves ThemeMode from `ObserveThemeUseCase`, loads/saves panel width, and calls `AppTheme(mode) { RectifyWindowShell(...) }` with stub slot content.

components.name: ThemeOverrideToggle
components.responsibility: Small status-bar control cycling System → Light → Dark, persisted via the existing `SetThemeUseCase`/`pref_theme` (FR-18/AC-35). Reuses existing `IconButton` + the already-present `Sun` icon; no new component needed.

components.name: SidePanelWidthPreferenceSource (data-preference-api/-impl)
components.responsibility: `pref_side_panel_width` Int (dp), default 320. Follows the existing `PreferenceSource<T>` shape (MutableStateFlow seeded from storage, write-through). The only new persisted value in this deliverable.

components.name: PaletteContrastTest (presentation-core-styling/commonTest)
components.responsibility: Computes WCAG 2.x relative-luminance contrast for every surface/ink and signal-on-surface pairing in BOTH shipped palettes and asserts >=4.5:1 text / >=3:1 non-text (NFR-11/AC-36/AC-40). Must live in this module's own test source set because `attributeLightColorPalette`/`attributeDarkColorPalette` are `internal`. Alpha tokens (line/line2/hover/seg/codeBg are rgba with alpha 0.035–0.14) must be composited over their base surface before measuring.

alternatives.title: A. Build in rectify-kmp AND relocate the `.pipeline/` SDD workspace into it (RECOMMENDED)
pros: Zero duplication of the design system: `presentation-core-styling` consumed as a plain project dependency, satisfying FR-19/AC-36 'unmodified' by construction rather than by discipline.

Reuses ~109 already-shipped presentation-core-ui components authored from the SAME style guide, including SidebarTabs, SegmentedButtonGroup, DeviceChip, CounterBadge, StatusLine, StatusPill, KeyCap — the toolbar and status bar are mostly assembly, not authoring.
The desktop runnable path already exists: `:desktop-application` → `initKoin()` → `runDesktopApp()`; `./gradlew :desktop-application:run` works today.
Theme persistence chain already exists end to end (pref_theme → ... → App.kt), so AC-35 is nearly free.
All conventions (convention plugins, explicitApi(), core/ vs source/, Koin load order, preview convention) are already enforced by the build — Stage 4 cannot drift.
Spec and code colocated in one git repo, so Stage 4 writes and Stage 5 tests in the same working tree.
cons: The pipeline's assumed working repository changes from `/Users/andrew-malitchuk/Documents/rectify` to `/Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-kmp` — a one-time `git mv .pipeline` (plus the PRD workspace already there) and an orchestrator path change.
rectify-kmp keeps Android + iOS targets this deliverable does not need; a bare `./gradlew check` would also build them.
rectify-kmp carries unrelated template features (onboarding/home/settings/about/splash, navigation, Room, localisation) that Rectify will eventually delete.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The Android/iOS targets are close to a non-cost: NFR-10 constrains what is SHIPPED, and only `:desktop-application`'s packaging produces a distributable; unused targets merely compile. Mitigate the slow-check concern by having Stage 5 run `:presentation-core-ui:desktopTest :presentation-core-styling:desktopTest` rather than `check`. The genuine cost is the one-time workspace relocation, which is cheap and permanent; the cost of NOT doing it (a forked design system) recurs forever.

alternatives.title: B. Fresh Gradle project in Documents/rectify, porting presentation-core-styling (or just the token files) as source
pros: Spec and code colocated with zero pipeline changes.
Clean, desktop-only build: no AGP, no Android SDK, no iOS targets, fast `check`.
cons: A real fork of the design system. AC-36 says tokens are adopted 'as-is, unmodified' — a copy satisfies that on day one and silently stops satisfying it on the first upstream edit, with nothing to detect the drift.

Porting only the token files is not enough in practice: the shell needs SidebarTabs/SegmentedButtonGroup/DeviceChip/CounterBadge/StatusLine/KeyCap/StatusPill/AppButton too, so the port grows from ~31 files to ~140 or you re-author components that already exist.
Re-establishes convention plugins, explicitApi(), preview conventions, Koin wiring and the multiplatform-settings desktop backend from scratch.
Two repos must be kept in sync by hand forever — the direct threat to NFR-9/AC-30/AC-36 the clarify stage already flagged.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Buys pipeline convenience with permanent design-system debt. Only correct if rectify-kmp is considered a throwaway template that Rectify must leave behind — but its presentation-core-* modules are already Rectify-specific, which argues the opposite.

alternatives.title: C. Documents/rectify as a fresh build consuming rectify-kmp via Gradle composite build (includeBuild)
pros: Single source of truth for tokens — no fork.
Technically viable: `includeBuild("../../StudioProjects/rectify-kmp")` with `dependencySubstitution` mapping a module coordinate onto `project(":presentation-core-styling")`.
cons: `presentation-core-styling` applies `dev.rectify.io.convention.feature`, which applies `com.android.kotlin.multiplatform.library` (AGP 9.4.1) and registers androidTarget + iosArm64 + iosSimulatorArm64 — the composite build drags the full Android SDK requirement and iOS target configuration into a 'desktop-only' project anyway, so option C's main claimed benefit evaporates.

Consuming a KMP module across a composite build requires the desktop variant to be resolved through Gradle metadata plus matching Kotlin (2.4.21), Compose (1.12.1) and JVM (21) versions on both sides — version skew between the two builds becomes a new, silent breakage class.
Brittle absolute/relative path coupling between two repos; IDE import is noticeably worse than a single project.
You still need presentation-core-ui's components, so you end up composite-including most of rectify-kmp — i.e. option A with extra indirection.
alternatives.tradeoffs: All the coupling of one repo with none of the simplicity. Would make sense only if presentation-core-styling were published to a Maven repository as a standalone artifact — it is not, and publishing infrastructure does not exist in rectify-kmp today.

alternatives.title: D. Promote rectify-poc into the real app
pros: Already runs; proves Compose Desktop + JVM 21 + window lifecycle.
`Devices.kt` (adb discovery, screenshot capture, hierarchy dump) is genuinely valuable — for the DOWNSTREAM device-discovery spec.
`:mcp-server` module exists for the downstream Resolve & Send spec.
cons: `Main.kt` uses `androidx.compose.material` (Material 2) and raw `Color(0xFF...)` literals — the exact two things `.claude/rules/design-tokens.md` forbids. Adopting it means deleting its UI wholesale.
No token system, no theme provider, no light/dark, no explicitApi(), no convention plugins, no package-layout split.
Kotlin 2.4.20 / Compose 1.12.1 vs rectify-kmp's Kotlin 2.4.21 — a small but real alignment step.
Its only unique asset (Devices.kt) is out of scope for THIS deliverable.
alternatives.tradeoffs: The poc is a liability as a UI template and an asset as a device-bridge reference. Correct treatment: do not promote it; port `Devices.kt` into rectify-kmp as a data module when the device-discovery spec runs, and let the poc's UI die.

alternatives.title: E. State: Orbit MVI ShellViewModel vs plain Compose state hoisting
pros: Orbit matches `.claude/rules/orbit-mvi.md`'s four-file shape used by all five existing feature screens, giving uniformity if the shell later grows device/session state.
cons: The orbit rule's own frontmatter scopes it to `presentation-feature-*/**`; the shell is a layout organism plus a window entry point, so the rule does not apply.
The shell has three fields, no async work, no navigation, no error states, no one-shot side effects — a Contract/ViewModel/Screen/Content quartet would be ceremony around `var activeTab by remember`.
A ViewModel also makes the shell un-previewable and un-reusable from `desktopMain` without Koin.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Plain hoisting now; if a downstream spec adds session/device state to the shell, that state belongs in THAT feature's Orbit ViewModel and is passed into the shell's slots — the shell stays stateless either way. Chosen: plain hoisting.

alternatives.title: F. Persistence: reuse multiplatform-settings chain vs a desktop-only java.util.prefs call
pros: The multiplatform-settings chain already exists and is already wired on desktop (`PreferencesSettings(Preferences.userRoot().node("dev.rectify.io"))`); theme costs zero new persistence code.
Keeps the presentation layer from reaching into storage directly, preserving the repo's data→domain→presentation layering and Koin load order.
cons: One new Int preference costs the full rote chain: PreferenceSource interface + Impl + model + mapper + ConfigureRepository methods + use cases + DI registration (~6 small files) for a single integer.
alternatives.tradeoffs: A direct `java.util.prefs` read from the window composable would be 2 lines but punches through three architectural layers in the one place every future developer looks first. Pay the 6 rote files once; they are mechanical for Stage 4. Chosen: reuse the existing chain.

techStack.reason: Matches the repo the shell is built in; supersedes the poc's 2.4.20 with no behavioural difference.
Operator-dictated and already configured in ApplicationConventionPlugin's desktopMain; macOS-only Skiko renderer satisfies NFR-10 by construction.
FR-19/AC-36/constraint: tokens read only from @Composable scope, never a literal Color(0x...).

techStack.choice: presentation-core-ui atoms/molecules/organisms (SidebarTabs, SegmentedButtonGroup, DeviceChip, CounterBadge, StatusLine, StatusPill, KeyCap, AppButton, StatusIndicator)
techStack.reason: Already authored from the same style guide; the shell assembles rather than re-authors.
Three fields, no async, no side effects; Orbit is scoped to presentation-feature-* modules.

techStack.choice: multiplatform-settings via the existing PreferenceSource chain; desktop backend `PreferencesSettings(Preferences.userRoot().node("dev.rectify.io"))`

techStack.reason: Desktop has no lifecycle callback; the repo's rule already fixes this call site and the data→domain→presentation load order.

techStack.choice: Native macOS decorations + JBR client properties `apple.awt.fullWindowContent` / `apple.awt.transparentTitleBar` on `window.rootPane`
techStack.reason: Gives the screenshot's traffic-lights-inside-the-toolbar look while the OS still draws and manages the buttons — no custom hit-testing, drag regions or fullscreen handling to implement or maintain.

techStack.choice: kotlin.test in commonTest, wired once in Library/Feature convention plugins; `./gradlew :<module>:desktopTest`
techStack.reason: testing.md says ZERO tests exist — this deliverable establishes the pattern, per-module wiring is explicitly discouraged.

exceptions: Panel width restored from preferences is outside [260,480] (corrupted/hand-edited prefs or a future bound change) → clamp on read with `clampPanelWidth`, never trust the stored value.

Preferences store unreadable/read-only (`java.util.prefs` can throw `BackingStoreException` on a locked or sandboxed profile) → fall back to defaults (ThemeMode.System, 320dp) and keep running; persistence failure must never block the window from opening.
`pref_theme` holds an unrecognised string (older/newer build) → the existing ThemePreferenceMapper already falls back; change that fallback from Light to System for FR-18/AS-5.
Window restored smaller than the minimum by the OS on a display-configuration change → re-apply `window.minimumSize` and let AWT clamp.
Cmd+1/2/3 pressed while the side panel is absent (no session) → no-op, do not mutate activeTab (SC-4/AC-33 presuppose a visible panel).

Window narrower than minimum would make stage + max panel overlap → stage uses `weight(1f)` so the panel keeps its width and the stage shrinks; at 1024dp with a 480dp panel the stage still has ~540dp, which is acceptable.
edgeCases: macOS system appearance changes while the app is running and mode == System → `isSystemInDarkTheme()` must recompose; verify on desktop/Skiko, as this is the one AS-3 assumption that is NOT proven by a shipped desktop build of rectify-kmp.
Drag handle double-click / zero-delta drag → must not write preferences; persist only on `onDragStopped` with a changed value (java.util.prefs writes on every frame would be pathological).
First run with no stored width → documented default 320dp (FR-21) and the panel must still obey the 260/480 clamp.
Session ends while the panel is open → panel unmounts (sidePanel = null); the last width must survive the unmount, so width lives in ShellState/prefs, not inside SidePanelFrame.
Session restarts → tab resets to Notes (AC-32), width does NOT reset (AC-39) — two different lifetimes in one state holder.

Alpha tokens (line/line2/hover/seg/codeBg are rgba 0.035–0.14) cannot be contrast-checked raw; they must be composited over their parent surface first, or the NFR-11 test produces meaningless numbers.

`pop` is deliberately dark in BOTH palettes (0xFF18191C light / 0xFF2C2D31 dark) — any contrast test must pair `pop` with on-pop ink, not with the theme's default ink, or light mode will report a false failure.
Traffic-light inset: with native decorations the shell must reserve ~78dp of leading space in the toolbar on macOS, otherwise the buttons overlap the platform switch.

Monospace tokens (JetBrains Mono per the style guide) must resolve on desktop — font loading is per-platform; verify `Theme.typography.monoMeta` renders mono in the desktop build, not a silent fallback.
HiDPI: `window.minimumSize` is an AWT `Dimension` in device-independent AWT units; confirm 1024x700 behaves on a 2x Retina display and is not silently halved/doubled.
implementationSteps: 0. Resolve survey Q1 (repository strategy). If 'relocate into rectify-kmp': `git mv` the `.pipeline/` workspace into rectify-kmp, record the new code root in the plan artifact, and point Stage 4/5 at it. Nothing else can start first.
1. Wire `kotlin.test` into `commonTest` once, inside LibraryConventionPlugin and FeatureConventionPlugin (per testing.md) — the repo's first test infrastructure.

2. Add `PaletteContrastTest` in `presentation-core-styling/src/commonTest` (internal palettes are only visible there): WCAG relative-luminance helper + alpha compositing + assertions over every surface/ink and signal-on-surface pair in both palettes (NFR-11/AC-36/AC-40). This is the cheapest high-value test and it de-risks the inspection-only ACs.
3. Add shell primitives to presentation-core-ui: `ShellTab`, `clampPanelWidth`, `shortcutToTab`, `rememberShellState` (+ their unit tests, AC-33/AC-38).
4. Add `PanelResizeHandle` (atom) and `StageSurface` (dotted-grid ground drawn from tokens).

5. Add `ShellToolbar` and `ShellStatusBar` organisms, assembled from the EXISTING SegmentedButtonGroup / DeviceChip / CounterBadge / AppButton / StatusIndicator / StatusLine / KeyCap components — no new leaf components unless something is genuinely missing.
6. Add `SidePanelFrame` reusing `SidebarTabs` with items Notes/Payload/History, defaulting to Notes (AC-32), content as a slot.

7. Add `RectifyWindowShell` composing 4-6, with the nullable `sidePanel` slot (AC-31/FR-15); add `@Preview` for the no-panel and with-panel states in both ThemeMode.Light and ThemeMode.Dark (AC-30/AC-31 inspection evidence).

8. Add the `pref_side_panel_width` chain: PreferenceSource api + impl + model, mapper, ConfigureRepository methods, Get/Set use cases, DI registration appended at the end of each layer group (Koin load order is significant).

9. Flip the theme default to System: rename `ThemeModel.MaterialU` → `ThemeModel.System` keeping its stored string value, and change App.kt's `initial`/null fallback from Light to System (FR-18/AS-5). Do NOT change `pref_theme`'s key.

10. Extend `runDesktopApp()`/add `RectifyWindow`: `rememberWindowState(size = DpSize(1240.dp, 820.dp))`, `window.minimumSize = Dimension(1024, 700)`, macOS full-size-content client properties, `onPreviewKeyEvent` → `shortcutToTab`, `AppTheme(mode) { RectifyWindowShell(...) }` with stubbed slot content (AC-34/AC-37).

11. Fill every slot with static stubs: 'Android | iOS' (Android selected), '● No device ▾', '⓪ staged', 'Clear', disabled 'Resolve & Send ⌘↵', status 'adb 35.0.1 · idb 1.1.8 · ready' / 'Rectify 0.4' — non-functional by design (AC-37).
12. Run `./gradlew :desktop-application:run`, compare against both cached screenshots in light AND dark, and record the inspection evidence for AC-12/AC-30/AC-31/AC-34/AC-36/AC-37/AC-40.
13. Amend the PRD's green-signal note from hue 152 to the shipped 150 (see openDecisions) so the two documents stop disagreeing.
gaps: No dark-theme design reference exists for the shell; both cached screenshots are light. The dark palette is shipped and adopted (AS-4), but the shell's dark appearance can only be validated against token correctness plus the automated contrast test — not against a design comp.

The three-tab side panel is entirely unillustrated (neither screenshot shows it). Its header height, padding, tab-row placement and divider treatment are being designed here from FR-11 + SidebarTabs' existing geometry (26dp tab height, 6dp radius), not copied from a comp. Flag for design review.
The 'bezel-less stage' dotted/grid texture has no specified cell size, dot radius or opacity token — it will be approximated from the screenshot and should become a named token if it survives review.

`presentation-core-ui`'s SidebarTabs example uses 'Annotations', while FR-11/AC-12 mandate 'Notes'. Confirm whether the kit component's example label or the spec wins (spec wins for this deliverable; the component takes labels as parameters, so no code conflict — but the naming divergence suggests the catalog may call the same tab two different things).

AS-3 (macOS system-appearance detection through `isSystemInDarkTheme()` on JVM/Skiko) is asserted as 'already proven by rectify-kmp' — rectify-kmp's AppTheme supports System, but there is no evidence anyone has observed a LIVE appearance switch in its desktop build. Verify early; a fallback would be reading `apple.awt.application.appearance` / an NSApplication observer, which is real work.
Zero tests exist in rectify-kmp, so there is no CI, no test task wiring and no coverage baseline. Stage 5 depends on step 1 above actually landing.
No macOS packaging (`nativeDistributions`/`packageDmg`) is configured in `:desktop-application` — out of scope for the shell, but the first thing missing for an actual macOS deliverable.
Monospace (JetBrains Mono) and SF Pro font availability in the desktop build is unverified; the typography tokens exist but desktop font resolution is untested.

No decision exists on what happens to rectify-kmp's template features (onboarding/home/settings/about/splash + Navigation3 + Room) once the shell becomes the app's root — the shell bypasses `NavigationHost`, leaving dead code paths.

risks.text: The pipeline's working repository (Documents/rectify) is not where the code should live; if the relocation is rejected, Stage 4 writes into an empty repo and the design system gets forked.
risks.mitigation: Make this survey Q1 and resolve it before any planning. If relocation is rejected, pick option C (composite build) over option B (source port) and add an automated token-drift check comparing the two palettes file-for-file.

risks.text: A ported/copied palette silently diverges from presentation-core-styling, breaking AC-36's 'unmodified' claim after the fact.
risks.mitigation: Avoid copying at all (option A). If copying is unavoidable, add a test that hashes the upstream LightColor.kt/DarkColor.kt content and fails on drift.

risks.text: `isSystemInDarkTheme()` does not react to a live macOS appearance change on JVM/Skiko, breaking FR-18's System mode.
risks.mitigation: Spike it in step 10 before building the toggle; fall back to a manual-override-only default if it proves static, and downgrade FR-18's System behaviour to launch-time detection with an explicit note.

risks.text: macOS traffic lights overlap the toolbar content, or the full-size-content client properties behave differently under a non-JBR JDK.
risks.mitigation: Reserve the leading inset unconditionally; if the client properties are unavailable, native decorations degrade to a standard title bar above the toolbar — ugly but functional and zero extra code.

risks.text: Writing the panel width on every drag frame thrashes `java.util.prefs` (which flushes to disk).
risks.mitigation: Persist only on `onDragStopped`, and only when the value actually changed.

risks.text: Establishing the repo's first test suite turns into a yak-shave (CI wiring, desktop test runtime, Compose UI test deps) and consumes Stage 5.

openDecisions.decision: Where the deliverable is built, and what happens to the `.pipeline/` SDD workspace (resolves clarify open question 4 and outOfScope item 8).
options: A: Build in rectify-kmp; relocate the `.pipeline/` workspace into it so spec and code share one repo
B: Fresh Gradle project in Documents/rectify; port presentation-core-styling in as source
C: Documents/rectify consuming rectify-kmp via Gradle composite build (includeBuild + dependencySubstitution)
D: Promote rectify-poc
openDecisions.recommendation: A. rectify-kmp already contains the token system AND ~109 Rectify-specific UI-kit components built from the same style guide, a working macOS desktop entry point, and a working desktop preference backend. B forks all of it and structurally endangers AC-36; C drags AGP/Android-SDK/iOS targets in anyway (presentation-core-styling applies the feature convention plugin) so it buys nothing over A; D's UI is Material 2 with hardcoded colors — exactly what design-tokens.md forbids.

openDecisions.decision: macOS window chrome: native traffic lights vs custom-drawn (resolves clarify open question 1).
options: Native decorations, standard title bar above the toolbar
Native decorations + JBR `apple.awt.fullWindowContent` / `apple.awt.transparentTitleBar` client properties, with a reserved ~78dp leading inset in the toolbar
undecorated = true with fully custom traffic lights
openDecisions.recommendation: Native + full-window-content client properties. It reproduces the screenshot's 'traffic lights sitting inside the toolbar' while the OS still draws, animates and manages the buttons (including fullscreen and window-drag behaviour) — roughly four lines in the FrameWindowScope versus a custom-chrome implementation nobody asked for. Degrades gracefully to a standard title bar if the properties are unsupported. Custom chrome means re-implementing hit-testing, drag regions, double-click-to-zoom and fullscreen — real work with no requirement behind it.

openDecisions.decision: Persistence key names (resolves clarify open question 2).
options: Reuse existing `pref_theme`; add `pref_side_panel_width` (Int, dp)
New namespaced keys (`pref_shell_theme`, `pref_shell_panel_width`)
A single serialized `pref_shell_state` JSON blob
openDecisions.recommendation: Reuse `pref_theme` + add `pref_side_panel_width`. The preferences rule states plainly that an existing key must never be renamed (it orphans stored values), and the `pref_<name>` convention is already established across pref_theme/pref_language/pref_onboarding_completed/pref_unit_system. A JSON blob breaks the typed PreferenceSource pattern for no benefit. Default width 320dp; both values live in the existing desktop node `dev.rectify.io`.

openDecisions.decision: The 2-degree OKLCH green hue discrepancy — PRD says oklch(0.66 0.15 152), shipped `sentFixed` says oklch(0.66 0.15 150) → Color(0xFF3EAB5E) (resolves clarify open question 3).
options: Shipped token (hue 150) is authoritative; amend the PRD note
PRD (hue 152) is authoritative; change LightColor.kt and DarkColor.kt
Leave both as-is and document the divergence
openDecisions.recommendation: Shipped token (150) is authoritative; amend the PRD note. AC-36 mandates adopting every signal token 'unmodified', so editing the palette to chase 2 degrees would itself violate the AC this deliverable is written against. At C=0.15 a 2-degree hue shift is sub-JND (imperceptible) and cannot change any contrast ratio meaningfully. The code is the working implementation, it is already consumed by both palettes identically (FR-23), and the trailing OKLCH comment keeps traceability. Fixing the document is free; fixing the code costs an AC violation.

options: Plain Compose state hoisting (rememberShellState)
Orbit MVI ShellViewModel (Contract/ViewModel/Screen/Content)
openDecisions.recommendation: Plain hoisting. orbit-mvi.md is scoped by frontmatter to `presentation-feature-*/**`; the shell is an organism + window entry point with three fields, no async, no navigation and no one-shot effects. A ViewModel would also make the shell un-previewable and unusable from desktopMain without Koin.

options: presentation-core-ui organism/shell/ + compose-application desktopMain window wiring (no new Gradle module)
A new `presentation-feature-shell` module following the Orbit four-file shape
A new `presentation-core-shell` module
openDecisions.recommendation: No new Gradle module. The shell is reusable UI (presentation-core-ui's stated purpose) plus entry-point wiring (compose-application's stated purpose). A new module adds a settings.gradle entry, a convention-plugin application, a Koin module and an iOS framework baseName for zero benefit — and a `presentation-feature-*` name would drag in the Orbit convention the shell does not need.

openDecisions.decision: Test scope for Stage 5, given the repo has zero tests today.
options: Pure-function unit tests + automated WCAG contrast assertions only (kotlin.test)
Add Compose UI tests via runComposeUiTest / ui-test-junit4
Inspection only, no automated tests
openDecisions.recommendation: Pure-function + contrast only. Runnable and real: `clampPanelWidth` (AC-38), `shortcutToTab` (AC-33), theme/width preference round-trip against an in-memory Settings (AC-35/AC-39), window-constant assertions (AC-34), tab-count assertion (AC-12), and the contrast sweep over both shipped palettes (NFR-11/AC-36/AC-40). Adding a Compose UI test harness to a repo with no test infrastructure at all is a Stage-5-consuming yak-shave for marginal coverage; rendering correctness is what the inspection ACs and the light/dark previews are for.

proposedSurvey.question: Where is this deliverable actually built, and what happens to the spec workspace? (THE decision — everything else depends on it)
options: Build in /Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-kmp AND relocate the .pipeline/ SDD workspace into that repo, so spec + code + design system share one git repo
Build in rectify-kmp but leave the .pipeline/ workspace in Documents/rectify (two repos; Stage 4/5 target rectify-kmp)
Build in Documents/rectify as a fresh Gradle project, porting presentation-core-styling (and the needed presentation-core-ui components) in as source
Build in Documents/rectify consuming rectify-kmp via a Gradle composite build (includeBuild + dependencySubstitution)
Promote rectify-poc into the real app and pull the token system into it
proposedSurvey.recommended: Build in /Users/andrew-malitchuk/StudioProjects/rectify-kmp AND relocate the .pipeline/ SDD workspace into that repo, so spec + code + design system share one git repo
proposedSurvey.rationale: rectify-kmp is not just a token file set: presentation-core-styling (AppTheme already resolving Light/Dark/System) sits next to presentation-core-ui's ~109 components authored from the SAME Rectify style guide — SidebarTabs (its own KDoc example is 'Annotations · Payload · History'), SegmentedButtonGroup (Android|iOS), DeviceChip ('● No device'), CounterBadge ('⓪ staged'), StatusLine, StatusPill, KeyCap ('⌘↵'). The macOS entry point (:desktop-application → initKoin() → runDesktopApp()) and the desktop preference backend (PreferencesSettings node dev.rectify.io, pref_theme end-to-end) already work. Porting (option 3) forks ~140 files and structurally breaks AC-36's 'adopted unmodified'; the composite build (option 4) still drags AGP 9.4.1, the Android SDK and the iOS targets in, because presentation-core-styling applies the feature convention plugin — so it costs more than option 1 and gains nothing; rectify-poc (option 5) is Material 2 with raw Color(0xFF...) literals, precisely what design-tokens.md forbids (keep only its Devices.kt, for the downstream device spec). Relocating .pipeline/ is one `git mv` and keeps Stage 4 writing and Stage 5 testing in the same tree as the code.

proposedSurvey.question: macOS window chrome / traffic-light treatment (clarify open question 1)
options: Native decorations with the standard macOS title bar sitting above the Rectify toolbar
Native decorations + macOS full-size-content window (apple.awt.fullWindowContent / transparentTitleBar) so the OS traffic lights sit inside the Rectify toolbar, with a reserved leading inset
Undecorated window with fully custom-drawn traffic lights
proposedSurvey.recommended: Native decorations + macOS full-size-content window (apple.awt.fullWindowContent / transparentTitleBar) so the OS traffic lights sit inside the Rectify toolbar, with a reserved leading inset
proposedSurvey.rationale: This is the only option that matches the cached screenshots (traffic lights inline with the platform switch) without hand-rolling window chrome. It is ~4 lines of rootPane client properties in the FrameWindowScope; the OS keeps drawing, animating and managing the buttons, including window drag, double-click-to-zoom and fullscreen. Custom chrome (option 3) means re-implementing all of that for a requirement nobody wrote; the plain title bar (option 1) is the safe fallback if the client properties misbehave under a non-JBR JDK.

proposedSurvey.question: Shell state management and module placement
options: Plain Compose state hoisting (rememberShellState) inside presentation-core-ui + compose-application — no new Gradle module
New presentation-feature-shell module following the repo's Orbit MVI four-file convention (Contract/ViewModel/Screen/Content)
New presentation-core-shell module with plain state hoisting
proposedSurvey.recommended: Plain Compose state hoisting (rememberShellState) inside presentation-core-ui + compose-application — no new Gradle module
proposedSurvey.rationale: The shell holds three values (activeTab, panelWidth, isSessionActive) with no async work, no navigation and no one-shot side effects. The orbit-mvi rule's own frontmatter scopes it to presentation-feature-*/**, so it does not apply to a layout organism; an Orbit quartet would be four files of ceremony around `var activeTab by remember`, and a ViewModel would make the shell un-previewable and unusable from desktopMain without Koin. A new Gradle module adds a settings entry, a convention-plugin application, a Koin module and an iOS framework baseName for zero benefit — presentation-core-ui is literally the repo's shared-component module and compose-application is literally its entry-point module.

proposedSurvey.question: Persistence for the two values that must survive restart (theme override, panel width)
options: Reuse the existing multiplatform-settings chain: keep pref_theme unchanged, add pref_side_panel_width (Int dp, default 320) through the full PreferenceSource → mapper → repository → use-case path
Reuse pref_theme for theme, but read/write the panel width directly from java.util.prefs in the window composable (2 lines, skips the layer chain)
Introduce new namespaced keys for both (pref_shell_theme, pref_shell_panel_width)
proposedSurvey.recommended: Reuse the existing multiplatform-settings chain: keep pref_theme unchanged, add pref_side_panel_width (Int dp, default 320) through the full PreferenceSource → mapper → repository → use-case path
proposedSurvey.rationale: pref_theme already works end to end on desktop (PreferencesSettings on node dev.rectify.io), so AC-35 costs only a default change from Light to System. The preferences rule forbids renaming an existing key — it silently orphans stored values — which rules out option 3. Option 2 is 2 lines but punches the presentation layer straight through to storage in the single most-copied file in the app; the ~6 rote files for one Int are mechanical for Stage 4 and keep data→domain→presentation intact. Write the width only on drag-end, never per frame — java.util.prefs flushes to disk.

proposedSurvey.question: What Stage 5 actually runs, given rectify-kmp has ZERO tests today
options: kotlin.test only: pure-function tests (clamp 260/480, Cmd+1/2/3 mapping, preference round-trip, window constants, three-tab assertion) PLUS an automated WCAG contrast sweep over both shipped palettes
The above plus Compose UI tests via runComposeUiTest / ui-test-junit4 (render the shell, click tabs, drag the handle)
No automated tests; all ACs verified by inspection against the screenshots
proposedSurvey.recommended: kotlin.test only: pure-function tests (clamp 260/480, Cmd+1/2/3 mapping, preference round-trip, window constants, three-tab assertion) PLUS an automated WCAG contrast sweep over both shipped palettes
proposedSurvey.rationale: testing.md confirms no test exists anywhere in rectify-kmp, so this deliverable establishes the pattern — wire kotlin.test once in the Library/Feature convention plugins, not per module. The contrast sweep is the standout: it turns AC-36/AC-40/NFR-11 from inspection-only into a real failing-or-passing check (it must live in presentation-core-styling's own commonTest, because both palettes are `internal`, and it must composite the alpha tokens line/line2/hover/seg/codeBg over their base surface and pair `pop` with on-pop ink, or it reports nonsense). Adding a Compose UI test harness to a repo with no test infrastructure at all is a Stage-5-consuming yak-shave; the shell's real logic is all pure, and rendering fidelity is what the inspection ACs and the light/dark @Preview pairs are for.
